climate.overview_html: NOAA now gives the El Niño about a 60% chance of becoming the strongest on record. COP31 in Antalya ended without a cover decision for the first time since 2009, and Copernicus logged a 2.12°C daily global anomaly.

items.headline: NOAA gives the 2026-27 El Niño about a 60% chance of becoming the strongest on record
items.summary: NOAA's latest update says the event is still strengthening, with sea surface temperatures off Ecuador and Peru nearly 5°C above normal.

items.headline: COP31 ends without a cover decision for the first time since 2009
items.summary: At least 32 countries rejected the final draft of the proposed Antalya Pact. Narrower texts on Article 2.1(c) and the Climate Finance Work Programme were adopted, along with a step to channel carbon-market revenue into the UN Adaptation Fund. None set a figure for tripling adaptation finance.

items.headline: Development banks announce finance side deals as COP31 deadlocks
items.summary: Development banks and governments announced new climate finance initiatives outside the formal negotiations. Decisions on the just transition mechanism were deferred to 2027.

items.headline: Copernicus records a 2.12°C daily global temperature anomaly
items.summary: Preliminary Copernicus data show 20 November 2026 ran 2.12°C above the pre-industrial average for the date, the largest daily anomaly measured. The record comes as El Niño heads toward a forecast peak in December.

major_events.name: Thanksgiving nor'easter, eastern US
major_events.status: Exiting; coastal flood risk into Saturday
major_events.impact: Record high tide at Bowers Beach, Delaware; major coastal flooding on the New Jersey shore with rescues in Atlantic City. Peak gusts near 78 mph; nearly one million customers lost power and more than 400 flights were cancelled. Forecasters expect coastal flood risk to persist into Saturday.

major_events.name: Southern Thailand monsoon rain
major_events.impact: Heavy rain forecast for 11 provinces on 27 November, with a low-pressure system possibly bringing heavier rain to the lower south on 29-30 November. Floods have already affected nearly 12,000 people in Phatthalung.

major_events.name: Queensland storms and Cape York heat
major_events.impact: Severe storms with heavy rain and damaging gusts are forecast from south-west to south-east Queensland through Sunday. A severe heatwave warning covers the Cape York Peninsula, with maxima in the mid-30s to low 40s °C.

weather.overview_html: The Thanksgiving nor'easter set a record high tide at Bowers Beach, Delaware, and pushed outages to nearly one million customers, including 171,000 in New Jersey. Southern Thailand begins a four-day flood alert with heavy rain in 11 provinces today. In Australia, severe storms are forecast across Queensland through the weekend.

items.headline: Nor'easter brings record coastal flooding to the Philadelphia region and Delaware
items.summary: Bowers Beach, Delaware, set a record high tide, and flooding closed Route 1 north of Bethany Beach. Utilities in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware reported more than 73,000 outages by midday Thursday.

items.headline: Storm cuts power to 171,000 New Jersey customers as gusts reach 78 mph
items.summary: New Jersey outages passed 171,000 on Thanksgiving evening under a statewide state of emergency. More coastal flooding was forecast with the next high tides.

items.headline: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million US customers without power
items.summary: Outages across the East Coast neared one million customers, and more than 400 US flights were cancelled on the holiday.

items.headline: Thanksgiving storm leaves flood and wind damage along the East Coast
items.summary: The storm's damage ran from the mid-Atlantic into the Northeast, with coastal flooding in New Jersey shore towns and downed trees inland.

items.headline: Thai Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rain in 11 provinces on 27 November
items.summary: Heavy rain is forecast for 11 provinces, mostly in the south, at the start of the 27-30 November flood alert. A low-pressure system may bring heavier rain to the lower south on 29-30 November.

items.headline: Severe storms forecast for Queensland through the weekend
items.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology expects severe storms from Friday in south-west Queensland, spreading to the south-east by Sunday with heavy rain and damaging gusts. It also forecasts a hot, dry summer under El Niño.

items.headline: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday by the storm
items.summary: Macy's moved its 100th parade to 8:30 a.m. Saturday, the first weather postponement in its history. NBC will air a rerun of the 2025 parade on Thursday.

items.headline: San Francisco sets a November water-level record above 8 feet
items.summary: The tide gauge hit 8.23 ft, beating the 7.97 ft November record from 1982. The NWS had warned king tides could reach the highest levels on record in some areas.

items.headline: Floods hit nearly 12,000 people in southern Thailand
items.summary: Mueang Phatthalung and Khuan Khanun are the hardest-hit districts. High tides and accumulated rain pushed Songkhla Lake into more than 100 homes.

items.headline: Sri Lanka forecasts more than 100 mm of rain in several provinces
items.summary: The Department of Meteorology expected heavy showers in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Uva and North-western provinces and in Galle and Matara districts.

renewables.overview_html: AEMO enters summer with 5.3 GW of new battery storage on the NEM and a forecast of warmer, drier weather under El Niño. South Australia's storm-hit Eyre Peninsula is due to reconnect by Friday on temporary towers. Egypt set a 31.9 GW renewables target for 2030 with 14.42 GWh of storage.

items.headline: AEMO counts on 5.3 GW of new batteries for a hot, dry El Niño summer
items.summary: AEMO's summer readiness release says more than 30 projects totalling 8.4 GW, including 5.3 GW of batteries, joined the NEM since December 2025. It expects sufficient supply under forecast conditions, with warmer and drier weather across most of Australia.

items.headline: Global residential storage shipments reach 57.58 GWh in the first nine months of 2026
items.summary: Home battery shipments worldwide totalled 57.58 GWh from January to September 2026.

items.headline: Egypt targets 31.9 GW of renewables and 14.42 GWh of storage by 2030
items.summary: Egypt set a 2030 goal of 31.9 GW of renewable capacity paired with 14.42 GWh of battery storage.

items.headline: Gambia signs a $68M deal for 52 MW of solar and 40.9 MWh of storage
items.summary: The $68 million project pairs 52 MW of solar with a 40.9 MWh battery.

items.headline: Eyre Peninsula to reconnect by Friday on temporary transmission towers
items.summary: Crews are building temporary towers after a storm downed two and damaged a third; permanent replacements could take up to a year. The 62 MW Cathedral Rocks wind farm stays offline and a rooftop solar export ban remains, as winds exceeded the towers' design limits.

items.headline: L&T wins a Rs 1,000-2,500 crore battery storage order at Khavda
items.summary: The Gujarat system will store surplus renewable output at high generation and release it at peak demand.

science.overview_html: No major AI weather model papers surfaced this holiday week. A test of Pangu, FengWu and FuXi on Oklahoma tornado environments remains the main ML item. New work links slower Atlantic overturning to a shrinking North Pacific low-oxygen zone in the ice age, and OceanICU estimates that without marine life, 2100 CO₂ would be 35-65% higher.

items.headline: Slower Atlantic overturning shrank the North Pacific's low-oxygen zone in the ice age
items.summary: Fossil shells from 11 sediment cores show the North Pacific oxygen minimum zone shrank, sometimes almost vanishing, during iceberg surges that slowed Atlantic overturning. The reconstruction carries a ±45% error margin and uses a coarse model.

items.headline: Ocean iodine will not offset future ozone pollution, study finds
items.summary: York and UEA researchers project that iodine's ozone-removing and cooling effects stall by 2100 and weaken slightly, even as Arctic Ocean iodine emissions rise 143%.
items.meta: University of York, UEA · Science Advances

items.headline: Without marine life, 2100 CO₂ would be 35-65% higher, OceanICU estimates
items.summary: A policy brief from the EU OceanICU project, presented at COP31, quantifies the biological carbon pump's role. It calls for caution and clear terms around proposed marine carbon dioxide removal.

items.headline: Study probes why India and southern China set heat records together in May 2026
items.summary: A team led by Gao Meng at Hong Kong Baptist University, with the Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences and NUIST, analyzed the intensity, duration and drivers of the concurrent heatwaves and assessed the human contribution.
items.meta: Hong Kong Baptist University · Advances in Atmospheric Sciences

items.headline: NOAA hurricane hunters log 480 flight hours across 10 cyclones in 2026
items.summary: AOML flew drones inside the eyewall of Hurricane Isaias and sampled Hurricane Polo, which peaked at 180 mph.

items.headline: Pangu, FengWu and FuXi tested on Oklahoma tornado environments
items.summary: Across ten strong-tornado events, Pangu-Weather handled storm-relative helicity well, while FuXi Weather did well on several thermodynamic parameters but overpredicted their magnitude.

items.headline: Ocean exchanges more kinds of gases with the atmosphere than assumed
items.summary: The authors say climate models miss part of this exchange and should account for seasonal changes in it.

items.headline: MIT method keeps AI models of chaotic systems physically bounded
items.summary: Researchers built physical constraints into machine-learning models of chaotic systems so predictions cannot run away to impossible values. Tests used standard benchmark systems, not operational weather or climate forecasts.

items.headline: Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify extreme precipitation under warming
items.meta: Wu, Tan, Liu et al. · Nature Climate Change
items.summary: Changes in how often several atmospheric phenomena occur together add to rising extreme-precipitation totals across much of eastern North America, eastern Asia and western Europe.

items.title: BBC switches its forecast supply back to the Met Office, replacing MeteoGroup
items.body_html: The BBC's Met Office partnership went live on 26 November, ending a supply deal with MeteoGroup, now part of DTN, that began in 2018. The BBC app and site add hourly 10-day forecasts and push alerts for Met Office warnings, and a BBC weather centre opens at the Met Office in Exeter.

items.title: ECMWF director cites Chongqing's Pangu-based rain warnings as a model
items.body_html: ECMWF's director visited Chongqing, where a Huawei-assisted AI model built on Pangu supports heavy-rainfall warnings up to six hours ahead. Chongqing's bureau already runs a 1 km hourly AI forecast for the Chengdu-Chongqing region.

items.title: Mesotech wins Air Force weather station contract worth up to $26.5M
items.body_html: Rancho Cordova-based Mesotech International won a five-year contract worth up to $26.5 million to maintain Air Force weather stations. Mesotech already holds a $31.3 million fixed-base weather system award from 2023.

items.title: SenseNet raises $43M to expand its wildfire detection network
items.body_html: Idealist Capital led the Series B financing, which mixes new equity, secondary sales and debt. SenseNet combines ground sensors, AI cameras, satellite data and predictive analytics, and says its monitored area grew from 130 million to over 450 million acres in a year.

items.title: Northrop Grumman wins $290.6M NASA contract for NOAA NEON microwave sounders
items.body_html: NASA awarded Northrop Grumman $290.6 million to build three Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications instruments for NOAA's Near Earth Orbit Network, with work running to April 2042. The government program of record sits alongside NOAA's commercial microwave-sounder data buys from Spire, Tomorrow.io and others.

items.title: SatSure raises $21M with investment from an Indian sovereign fund
items.body_html: Indian Earth observation analytics firm SatSure closed a $21 million Series B of equity, debt and secondaries, with India's sovereign space-tech fund investing. Its subsidiary KaleidEO has flight-tested an optical payload but has not yet launched a satellite.
